newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short stg vols spike after robust UK data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short stg vols spike after robust UK data.

text.p: UK data showing robust economic growth pushed up implied volatility of short sterling options on Wednesday as the underlying futures tumbled, traders said.
"It's carnage in the short sterling (futures) pit," said a trader at a British bank in London. "Daily volume is usually between 50,000 and 70,000 a day. We'd already done over 100,000 by 11 o'clock."
June short sterling futures were off 0.11 at 93.39 by 1232 GMT, while September futures were down 0.14 at 93.13.
Brokers quoted volatility of June short sterling options at 9.5 percent, September at 11.7 percent and December at 12.8.
They were all up about 0.2 from the previous close.
British unemployment fell 68,200 in February, while average earnings were up 5.0 percent in January. Retail sales were up 0.5 percent month-on-month.

Traders said although some of the figures had been leaked to a national newspaper, there had been little impact at the opening bell, as most market participants had awaited the actual release before reacting.
"You can't really afford to believe some tabloid on figures as important as these, this close to the election," said a booth manager at a Swiss house on the LIFFE floor.
March short sterling futures and options expire this session.

Short sterling options were trading briskly, with put options easily dominating trade. More than 7,000 June puts were traded at strikes from 92.75 to 93.50, and more than 4,000 puts in December, with 92.75 to 93.25 strikes popular.
Gilts options were less involved in the turmoil -- with May volatility rising to 7.8 percent from 7.6 percent, June to 8.0 percent from 7.9 percent, and September to 8.2 percent from 8.0 percent.
"There has yet to be signs that the election has really caught up with options," said a trader at a Swiss house. "It'll take a couple of weeks before volatility starts to rise."
He said the 10 percent level was a medium-term target, although volume has remained light.
